heading.purpose: Section titles, page headings. Bold but not heavy.

label.purpose: Category labels, table headers, chip text. Uppercase in schedule grid headers.

mono.purpose: Time cells, NRC codes, technical identifiers.

shadows.name: subtle
shadows.purpose: Minimal lift for chips, small elements.

shadows.name: default
shadows.purpose: Cards, containers. Present but not attention-grabbing.

shadows.name: glow
shadows.purpose: Atmospheric background effect only — never on interactive elements.

schedulePalette.description: Pastel colors for course blocks in the schedule grid. One color per distinct course, cycling through the palette.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Inverted button — light bg on dark canvas. Used for primary CTAs.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5rem; padding: 12px 20px; border-radius: 14px; background: #e4e7eb; color: #0a0d14; font-weight: 600; font-family: 'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 0.95rem; border: 1px solid #e4e7eb; cursor: pointer; transition: all 200ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #8895b3; border-color: #8895b3; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.4; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Surface-toned button for less critical actions.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5rem; padding: 8px 14px; border-radius: 14px; background: #161b27; color: #e4e7eb; font-weight: 500; font-family: 'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 0.9rem; border: 1px solid #232a39; cursor: pointer; transition: all 200ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: #1c2230; border-color: #2d3548; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Transparent button for tertiary actions. Appears on hover only.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5rem; padding: 8px 14px; border-radius: 14px; background: transparent; color: #e4e7eb; font-weight: 500; font-family: 'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 0.9rem; border: 1px solid transparent; cursor: pointer; transition: all 200ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: #1c2230; }

components.name: Card
components.description: Standard content container with tonal depth and subtle border.
components.html:
Título de sección

Contenido de la tarjeta aquí.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #161b27; border: 1px solid #232a39; box-shadow: 0 1px 3px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.4), 0 1px 2px -1px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.3); border-radius: 14px; padding: 16px; } .ds-card-title { font-weight: 700; font-size: 1.25rem; line-height: 1.3; color: #e4e7eb; margin: 0 0 8px 0; } .ds-card-body { font-size: 15px; line-height: 1.6; color: #9ba3b0; margin: 0; }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Standard text input with elevated background and focus glow.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; padding: 10px 12px; border: 1px solid #232a39; border-radius: 6px; background: #11151f; color: #e4e7eb; font-family: 'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 0.95rem; transition: all 200ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: #6b7a99; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(107, 122, 153, 0.12); } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #5e6675; }

components.name: Optional Chip

narrative.overview: The ecosystem aspires to feel like a well-organized academic workspace — serious enough to trust with consequential decisions (your semester schedule matters), but warm enough to stay in for an hour without fatigue. Technical elegance is the guiding aesthetic: precision in layout and information hierarchy, with a subtle warmth that comes from the gold accent and muted, human-friendly color choices. The dark theme is not 'dark mode as afterthought' — it's the native habitat, designed for late-night study sessions where the interface recedes and the data leads.
keyCharacteristics: Muted, desaturated palette — no neon, no saturated primaries; every color earns its place
Tonal layering over heavy shadows; depth comes from background hierarchy, not drop shadows
Warm gold accent as the single point of visual energy — used sparingly, never overwhelming
Typography-first hierarchy; information density without clutter
Shared token vocabulary across all apps; UniHorario's visual language is the ecosystem standard

rules.name: The Gold Accent Rule
rules.body: Warm Gold appears on ≤15% of any given screen. Its rarity is the point — it draws the eye to what matters most (category chips, accent highlights) without competing with the data.

rules.name: The Muted Palette Rule
rules.body: Every color in this system is desaturated by at least 30% from its pure hue. If a color looks vibrant, it's wrong. The palette earns trust through restraint.

rules.name: The No-Caps Exception Rule
rules.body: Text is never ALL CAPS except schedule grid day/time headers and category chip labels. When caps appear, they carry structural meaning — not decoration.

rules.name: The Tonal Layer Rule
rules.body: Depth is communicated through background color hierarchy (bg → bg-elevated → surface), not through shadows alone. Shadows reinforce what the tonal layering already suggests.

dos: Do use the tonal layer hierarchy consistently: bg → bg-elevated → surface. Never skip a layer.
Do keep Warm Gold reserved for accent moments — category chips, highlight states, subtle emphasis.
Do use Plus Jakarta Sans for all UI text. JetBrains Mono only for time codes and NRC numbers.
Do use ambient shadows at their documented intensities. Never add glow, neon, or colored shadows.
Do keep schedule grid cells at 56px height and 110px min-width.
donts: Don't use saturated or vibrant colors. Every color in this system is muted.
Don't add decorative borders, double lines, or dashed borders.
Don't use ALL CAPS outside schedule grid headers and category chips.
Don't add hover animations that transform scale or add dramatic shadows.
Don't introduce new color families without mapping them to an existing tonal role.
Don't use the primary color (steel blue) for large background fills.
